prompt:
Use case: compositing / precise-object-edit.
Edit target: the supplied original cozy viewing nook. Adapt this SAME scene into a very tall portrait phone background, 9:19.5 aspect ratio, approximately 1024 by 2216. Output the artwork only, no UI, text, logos or watermark.
Preserve: the same deep charcoal sofa, warmly lit oatmeal knitted throw, shaded amber lamp to the left, walnut side table with mug, plants, slippers, and nighttime window. Preserve the cozy material treatment, colors, soft light and familiar objects. Do not turn it into a new room or a product sculpture.
Change: replace the transparent cutout with a complete continuous dark room around it. Extend/outpaint the scene upward into quiet near-black charcoal wall and downward into a dim continuous floor. The furniture is now an immersive environment rather than a floating vignette. No circular base or isolated rug-shaped cutout edge.
Composition for the real app: keep the upper HALF mostly empty graphite wall, extremely dim and low-detail, so the brand mark, wordmark and one line of copy will read clearly. The sofa fills the lower middle of the portrait frame, roughly y=60% to y=82%, with its width held safely inside the middle 70% of the canvas. Place the warm lamp shade at the far-left edge around y=55%, and the window on the right around y=53% to y=68%, both muted. Cozy warm light settles on blanket and cushions. The bottom 15% is dark quiet floor for a sign-in button. Avoid placing bright objects or window highlights around the center upper half.
Palette: near-black #09090B, deep charcoal #242428, dark walnut and gentle honey-amber light, warm ivory texture, tiny muted coral accent. Keep the room restful, calm and premium. No strong spotlight beams or glow fog, no neon, no saturated colors, no new people or characters, no TV content, no known IP.
Output must be fully opaque, high-resolution tall portrait background. It should fill an iPhone welcome screen edge to edge with no frame, tile, cutout boundary or baked-in UI.
request: User requested same scene as background backdrop instead of inline illustration
